title: NO and NC contacts: a stop button that fails safe
summary: Learn the normally open and normally closed contacts, why a stop button is wired normally closed, and read a field stop signal correctly in a program that also lights a lamp when the stop circuit is open.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real stop button is wired: the scenario sets the stop signal for you.
objectives: Explain why a stop button is wired normally closed, and what a field NC button looks like to the program: TRUE at rest, FALSE when pressed or when the wire breaks.
Choose the right kind of contact in a rung: a normally open contact passes power when its variable is TRUE, a normally closed contact when it is FALSE.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/NcStop.ld.json two rungs are drawn. The first drives Motor from StartButton and StopButton. The second lights StopLamp when the stop circuit is open. StopButton is a stop button wired normally closed: it is TRUE at rest. Both rungs read it the wrong way. Make Motor run only while the stop circuit is closed, and StopLamp light only while it is open.
stages.checkpoint: You can say what value StopButton has at rest, when it is pressed and when its wire is cut.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict Motor and StopLamp. Start is held from {{t:40}} ms. Stop is pressed at {{t:50}} ms and released at {{t:60}} ms. What are Motor and StopLamp at {{t:50}} ms and at {{t:60}} ms?
stages.checkpoint: {{v:NcStop.Motor=false,NcStop.StopLamp=true@50|Motor OFF, lamp ON}} at {{t:50}} ms; {{v:NcStop.Motor=true,NcStop.StopLamp=false@60|Motor ON, lamp OFF}} at {{t:60}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program reads StopButton the wrong way in both rungs, so Motor never runs and StopLamp is lit at {{t:0}} ms with the stop circuit intact. Change it so that, with Start held, Motor runs while StopButton is TRUE and stops at {{t:50}} ms when it goes FALSE, and StopLamp is ON exactly while StopButton is FALSE. Leave StartButton, Motor and StopLamp as they are.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, which sets StartButton and StopButton the way the field devices would, and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named NcStop and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:40}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:60}} ms: Start stays pressed the whole time, but Motor falls at {{t:50}} ms when StopButton goes FALSE and returns at {{t:60}} ms. StopLamp is the mirror image of the stop circuit.
stages.checkpoint: Motor falls once at {{t:50}} ms, and Motor and StopLamp are never ON together.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: At {{t:70}} ms Start is released and StopButton is FALSE at the same time. Imagine that FALSE came from a cut wire instead of a button. What does the machine do, and why is that good?
stages.checkpoint: A cut wire reads like a press, so the motor stops and the lamp lights: the most common failure gives the stop, which is why stop buttons are wired normally closed.

hints.text: Look at the value StopButton has at rest and when Stop is pressed, and at what each of the two rungs must do in each case.

In the motor rung, replace the normally closed contact on StopButton with a normally open one. In the lamp rung, replace the normally open contact on StopButton with a normally closed one. Leave StartButton, Motor and StopLamp as they are.

faultCases: The starting program reads StopButton the wrong way in both rungs, so Motor never runs and StopLamp is lit at {{t:0}} ms with the stop circuit intact.
